correctness.rationale: For p,q>=2 independent parts of sizes a,b>=1, group-averaging any symmetric row-stochastic zero-diagonal nonnegative kernel over within-part and same-size part permutations does not increase centered operator norm. The invariant family has one variable x=qb w_AB in [0,min(1,1/r)], r=pa/(qb), and exact nonconstant eigenvalues -(1-x)/(p-1), -(1-rx)/(q-1), and 1-(1+r)x plus zeros. Thus SLEM is max of three affine absolute-value branches; decreasing-vs-increasing minimax gives unique invariant x*=min(cap,max(p/(p+(p-1)r),q/(q-1+qr))). This yields four exact r-phases with boundaries 1/q,p/q,p; global optimality follows by convex averaging, not uniqueness of all global kernels. Independent exact-rational scalar minimax on 6 parameter configurations and 501-point rational grids reproduced the branches and boundary deletion patterns; a finite grid cannot prove global optimality, supplied convex proof does.
